articles.title: Indians continue to shine at Shooting World Championships as Niraj Kumar, Aishwary Tomar reach 50m Rifle 3 Positions final
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India continued its impressive run at the ISSF World Championships 2026 as Niraj Kumar and Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar booked their places in
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India continued its impressive run at the ISSF World Championships 2026 as Niraj Kumar and Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar booked their places in the final of the men's 50m Rifle 3 Positions event.Niraj topped the qualification round with a score of 591-29x, while Aishwary secured fourth place with 586-27x, ensuring that both Indian shooters advanced to the final. Their teammate Akhil Sheoran also contributed to India's success as the trio claimed the bronze medal in the team competition.In another major achievement, Esha Singh, Manu Bhaker and Divya Thadigol Subbaraju captured the women's 25m pistol team gold medal at the championship in Doha.The Indian team recorded a combined score of 1761-68x, finishing ahead of the Republic of Korea (1748-66x), which took silver, and Vietnam (1745-54x), which settled for bronze.Esha led the Indian contingent with an impressive 590-25x, while Manu scored 587-24x and Divya contributed 584-19x. Both Esha and Manu also qualified for the individual final. Manu narrowly missed out on a medal, finishing fourth with 27 hits, while Esha secured eighth position with 11 hits.India added another medal to its tally through the men's 50m Rifle 3 Positions team event. Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar, Akhil Sheoran and Niraj Kumar combined for a score of 1751-91x to claim bronze.Czechia won the gold medal with 1754-92x, while Norway finished second with 1752-81x. Aishwary was India's leading scorer with 587-33x, followed by Niraj (582-31x) and Akhil (582-27x).The focus now shifts to November 11, when Niraj and Aishwary will compete in the men's 50m Rifle 3 Positions final, with India hoping to add another medal to its collection.India's overall performance at the ISSF World Championships has been impressive, with several shooters delivering podium finishes across different events. Niveditha Veloor Nair secured bronze in the women's 25m standard pistol, while Jaypal Malviya earned silver in the men's 10m air pistol.The men's 50m pistol team comprising Ravinder Singh, Saurabh Chaudhary and Amanpreet Singh won gold. Ravinder further strengthened India's medal tally by claiming individual silver in the same discipline.In the women's 10m air rifle team event, Elavenil Valarivan, Sonam Maskar and Shambhavi Kshirsagar also contributed to India's success by winning silver.With multiple medals across team and individual competitions, the Indian shooting contingent continues to make a strong statement on the international stage at the ISSF World Championships 2026.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: La denuncia del atleta paralímpico Alberto Ávila: "Un acosador amenaza con reventarme y asesinar a mi madre"
articles.standfirst: El madrileño atiende a MARCA. Lleva desde mayo sufriendo acoso a través de las Redes sociales. El caso ya está en manos de las autoridades. Sospecha de alguien de su entorno
articles.summary: El madrileño atiende a MARCA. Lleva desde mayo sufriendo acoso a través de las Redes sociales. El caso ya está en manos de las autoridades. Sospecha de alguien de su entorno
articles.body: Alberto Ávila lleva desde mayo sufriendo acoso a través de sus Redes sociales, en las que acumula un millón y medio de seguidores entre TikTok e Instagram. El tono del acosador ha ido subiendo cada vez más hasta recibir amenazas contra su integridad física y la de su madre. El atleta paralímpico, que fue el primer concursante de Supervivientes con discapacidad, ya ha puesto en manos de las autoridades el caso. También lo ha denunciado en sus redes sociales. El madrileño atiende a MARCA para explicar lo sucedido. "Todo empezó a principios de mayo cuando una chica que conocía me dijo que le habían escrito por Redes diciéndole que nos habían visto juntos, que si yo tenía novia (no era verdad)... No le di importancia, pensé que era algo puntual. Pero se empezó a repetir este mismo patrón cada vez que empezaba a seguir a una chica en Instagram. Esa persona está obsesionada con las chicas a las que sigo", relata. Empezó a mosquearse cuando a finales de mayo ya eran eran cinco las chicas que le habían avisado de que una persona les había escrito diciéndole barbaridades sobre Alberto. "Siempre dejándome a mí como un guarro. Incluso les decía que me había visto traficando con drogas (que obviamente no es verdad), que soy un acosador…", rememora a MARCA. Y nos envía los pantallazos que lo demuestran. En su grupo de entrenamiento estaba su ex novia y el novio actual de ésta y ella le contó que también la estaba acosando a ella. El tono del acosador o acosadora, porque no sabe su género, fue subiendo con el paso del tiempo. En junio ya le amenazó directamente. “Me escribió: 'Sé dónde vives, ten huevos a salir a la calle que te voy a reventar. Voy a asesinar a tu madre”, confiesa. Y pasó de escribir a las chicas de su entorno a ampliar a su círculo más cercano para sonsacarles información. También le han llegado mensajes insultándole por su físico. "Cojito paleto. Deforme...". Ávila nació sin peroné, con una malformación de la pierna derecha. "Tiene de 30 a 40 cuentas falsas. Ha habido días que se ha creado tres cuentas en una hora. Yo no le doy bola, pero mis amigos o amigas que le han contestado han llegado a recibir 20 mensajes en 10 minutos", revela. Alberto alguna vez le ha respondido desde alguna cuenta falsa o de una amiga provocándole para sonsacarle información y una vez estuvo a punto de quedar en persona. Sospecha que es alguien de su entorno. "Sabe demasiados detalles de mi vida privada que es imposible que los conozca aunque me siga en Redes Sociales", cuenta. Porque en su perfil, Ávila no relata cada detalle de su vida sino que usa las Redes para normalizar y visibilizar la discapacidad a través del sentido del humor. Da algunos detalles que muestran el grado de obsesión de esa persona hacia él. "El 17 de septiembre salí por una discoteca en Segovia con dos amigos. Era un jueves, no lo sabía nadie porque yo no subí a mis redes nada de esa noche. Pues el acosador sabía que estaba allí porque al día siguiente me envió una foto diciéndome que me tenía vigilado", confiesa. A raíz de subir el vídeo a Instagram en el que mandaba un mensaje directamente a su acosador, le han escrito "un montón de chicas a las que llevo 5 ó 10 años sin ver, que a ellas también las había escrito". "Está denunciado, no le tengo miedo y sé que le van a acabar pillando tarde o temprano", avisa Ávila.

articles.title: 'I was looking forward to be in Magnus Carlsen's group': Vaishali after winning two blitz games against super GMs
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian Grandmaster Vaishali Rameshbabu made an impressive start at the inaugural Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot in Budapest,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian Grandmaster Vaishali Rameshbabu made an impressive start at the inaugural Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot in Budapest, defeating two well-known grandmasters, Hans Niemann and Wesley So, in the opening blitz event.Her victories were particularly significant as she is one of only two women competing in a 24-player field featuring some of the world's best chess players.Vaishali defeated Niemann in the first round before beating So in the third. Her win against So was especially impressive, as the American had recently claimed his fourth US Championship title.She eventually finished the nine-round blitz event with four points out of nine."I was looking forward to be in Magnus's group. It's a very strong group like Arjun, Wesley, MVL. I mean what a what a group this is. Yeah, it's going to be a lot of challenge. I'm looking forward," Vaishali told ChessBase India.Carlsen takes the lead in blitz eventMeanwhile, five-time world champion Magnus Carlsen dominated the opening event, finishing unbeaten with seven points from nine rounds. France's Maxime Vachier-Lagrave secured second place with 6.5 points, while Levon Aronian finished third with six points.Carlsen's final-round victory over Haik Martirosyan helped him secure the top spot. His strong finish also gives him an advantage in the next stages, as the tournament rules allow higher finishers to get better tiebreak positions and certain advantages in knockout matches.India's Arjun Erigaisi also had a promising run, defeating Vachier-Lagrave and Fabiano Caruana. However, a final-round loss to Aronian meant he finished with 5.5 points.Group stage brings a bigger challengeThe tournament will now move to the Fast Classic format, where 24 players will be divided into four groups of six. Each game will have 45 minutes on the clock, with an additional 30 seconds per move. A win will earn three points, while a draw will give each player one point.Vaishali and Bibisara Assaubayeva will compete in Group D alongside Vachier-Lagrave, Erigaisi, Niemann and So. Only the winners of the four groups will qualify for the main knockout stage.The $650,000 tournament is being organised as a pilot for a proposed world chess tour that will combine classical, rapid and blitz formats.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Newly married wrestler set for huge opportunity? 5 female WWE stars who can win The John Cena Classic
articles.summary: WWE is set to witness The John Cena Classic, a unique competition between WWE and NXT stars for the Cena Classic title.
articles.body: WWE is set to witness The John Cena Classic, a unique competition between WWE and NXT stars for the Cena Classic title. It will take place on December 14 at Disney World, in Orlando, Florida. As John Cena revealed, there will be separate competitions for the men’s and women’s divisions. So far, only one female WWE star has been invited to the John Cena Classic; however, more talented women will be eyeing that same opportunity. So, here are five WWE superstars from the women’s division that can win the Cena Classic.5. Roxanne PerezRoxanne Perez has been garnering momentum since coming up to the main roster last year. She has won the WWE Women’s Tag Team titles, been a part of Judgment Day, and has delivered impressive matches, especially in AAA. With The Prodigy looking for her breakout, a victory in The John Cena Classic could be the opportunity she needs to begin her rise as a top singles competitor.4. Kendal GreyKendal Grey has made a significant impact in a very short tenure in NXT. Her impressive personality and in-ring acumen led her to become the NXT Women’s Champion within months of her debut. With Grey returning to NXT after a brief hiatus, she could be a top candidate from the brand to win the Women’s John Cena Classic.3. Sol RucaSol Ruca got called up to the main roster this year after a spectacular stint in NXT. In just a few months of her debut, she defeated Becky Lynch to win the Women’s Intercontinental title and has been featured in top matches for months. Therefore, Ruca has the potential to win the John Cena Classic and gain huge momentum from the victory to ascend further.2. Kelani JordanKelani Jordan became the first female WWE star to be invited by John Cena for the John Cena Classic. The newly married Mrs. Carmelo Hayes has lived up to her moniker of being The Standout and is the reigning NXT Women’s Champion. With huge momentum and endorsement by Cena himself, she can be a top pick to win the entire John Cena Classic.1. IYO SkyA major name from the WWE main roster to win the John Cena Classic is IYO Sky. The Genius of the Skies is a top star in every sense. However, she has been out of the Women’s title picture for a while. Yet, she is still at the top of her game in the ring and could use it to win the competition and get back her spot at the top of the women’s division.Also read: Roman Reigns will set an incredible record at WWE Survivor Series 2026Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Four-star center commits to UConn men’s basketball, adding to strong ’27 class
articles.summary: The 2027 recruiting class is getting even stronger for the UConn men’s basketball program. Jack Thelen, a four-star, 7-foot-1 center from Osseo, Minnesota, a...
articles.body:
The 2027 recruiting class is getting even stronger for the UConn men's basketball program.

Jack Thelen, a four-star, 7-foot-1 center from Osseo, Minnesota, and Maple Grove High, announced his commitment to the Huskies via Rivals on Wednesday afternoon.

Thelen initially committed to Wisconsin in June but reopened his recruitment after seeing his stock rise over the summer. He averaged 8.5 points and 6.7 rebounds per game on the Adidas 3SSB circuit and climbed to the No. 16-ranked center in the class by 247Sports, No. 15 by ESPN . He's ranked No. 111 in the class in the 247Sports composite rankings.

Thelen earned an offer from Dan Hurley and staff after visiting Storrs on Oct. 29, and then visited Illinois on Nov. 7 before making his decision.

Thelen is the fourth recruit to choose UConn in the 2027 class, joining No. 10 recruit NaVorro Bowman Jr., a 6-foot-3 guard, and No. 11 recruit Jordan Page, a 6-foot-5 wing. The Huskies also landed a 6-foot-10 French center, Keny Vado, according to a report from Jonathan Givony earlier this month.

The four-man class ranks third nationally by 247Sports , behind only LSU and Houston.

"Thelen is a big bodied lefty with real size and a quality motor," 247Sports Director of Scouting, Adam Finkelstein, wrote . "He's got a definite competitive streak, is vocal on the defensive end, and willing to use his body in the lane. While he is sometimes content to trot the floor hunched over, he's not as vulnerable when pulled to the perimeter defensively as expected. Offensively, he doesn't appear to need a certain number of touches or shots to stay engaged. He has good hands, soft touch in the paint, both hands around the rim (albeit with a lower release point), is physical in the post, and reliable reversing the ball on the perimeter. While he's not looking to shoot out there yet, his 82% free-throw shooting is encouraging, even on very low volume (under 2 attempts per game)."

articles.title: Ex-Red Sox Reliever, Braves World Series Champion Retires After 11-Year MLB Career
articles.summary: Chris Martin has retired after 11 seasons in the big leagues
articles.body:
Longtime reliever Chris Martin has retired after 11 seasons in the big leagues, according to MLB insider Robert Murray.

Martin pitched for seven organizations, but spent the most time with the Texas Rangers. He also pitched for the Colorado Rockies, New York Yankees, Atlanta Braves, Chicago Cubs, Los Angeles Dodgers and Boston Red Sox.

Martin won a World Series with the Braves in 2021, pitching in five games during their run to the Fall Classic. He allowed just one run that postseason across 4 1/3 innings. He pitched in three postseasons for the Braves and one for the Dodgers.

The Rockies drafted Martin in 2005, but he did not make his debut until 2014, at 27 years old. He appeared in 16 games that season and was traded to the Yankees before the 2015 season. The Yankees released him after the 2015 season, and he spent the 2016 and 2017 seasons in Japan.

He appeared in 92 games for the Nippon-Ham Fighters in two seasons. In 2016, he had a 1.07 ERA, and in 2017 he had a 1.19 ERA. He signed with the Rangers before the 2018 season.

Since 2018, he has pitched in 394 games and posted a 3.26 ERA. He carved out a successful role as a reliever and even received Cy Young Award votes in 2023, when he was a member of the Red Sox.

The 40-year-old appeared in 16 games for the Rangers and pitched 14 innings. He had a 9.00 ERA, and now he has decided to hang it up.

In 2025, he posted a 2.98 ERA in 49 games, so his falloff was somewhat of a surprise. Regardless, his time in the big leagues has finally come to an end. He finished his career with a 3.53 ERA and pitched in a total of 434 games.

articles.title: Leon football Hall of Fame celebrates 50 years of history, tradition
articles.summary: Leon High School marks 50 years of its unique football Hall of Fame, a tradition started by coach Gene Cox.
articles.body:
For Kurt Unglaub , the significance of Leon High's Football Hall of Fame isn't simply the hundreds of former Lions who have been honored the past 50 years.

It's that the tradition started by legendary Leon football coach Gene Cox has endured.

While many similar programs have disappeared or evolved into broader athletic halls of fame, Leon's remains devoted solely to football and the people who built its tradition.

"Us being able to keep it going for 50 years, it's just been a work and just a blessing," Unglaub said. "I want you to know that, a huge blessing. … Fifty years of anything's pretty good."

That longevity will be celebrated Thursday at The Moon, where more than 300 people are expected to gather, including more than 80 Hall of Famers and dozens of former cheerleaders.

High school football changes. Coaches leave. Players grow older. But for five decades, the Leon Football Hall of Fame has kept its history, and the people who made it, connected.

"I don't know of any Hall of Fames in the state of Florida that have lasted that long," said Leon football coach Ricky Bell, one of three generations of his family in the Hall along with his father and son, Lions athletic director Riley Bell. "This has survived because it was set up the way it was set up in the beginning. And I think that really was some foresight on Gene Cox's thinking, so it would last and last."

Leon football Hall of Fame stirs fond memories

One reason Leon's football Hall of Fame is still going strong after 50 years can be traced to the way Cox helped structure it from the beginning.

Instead of tying the Hall's future to whoever happened to be Leon's head football coach, Cox helped establish an organization with its own officers, rotating leadership and regular meetings. That allowed new generations of former players and supporters to take ownership and keep the tradition alive through coaching and administrative changes.

Unglaub, a longtime member and former three-year president of the Leon Football Hall of Fame, was asked by the board to return as chairman of the 50th anniversary celebration.

He stressed that Thursday's event isn't a formal Hall of Fame ceremony but a reunion, bringing generations of Leon football players, coaches, cheerleaders and supporters back together.

Adding to the significance, Gene Cox's son, Alan, is serving as the board's president during the 50th anniversary year of a Hall of Fame that features more than 280 inductees.

"There's an 80-year-old cheerleader who is coming," Unglaub said. "We're not having a banquet. This is just a fun party. A celebration is what it is."

The 2026 season marks 110 years of the program, highlighted by a historic 37–31 double-overtime win against rival Lincoln High School that snapped a 27-year losing streak to the Trojans.

articles.title: Aday Mara’s Strong Development Defends Against OKC Injuries
articles.summary: Aday Mara is on the rise for the Oklahoma City Thunder this season, and the team hopes that he can continue his development throughout the campaign. Suddenly...
articles.body:
Aday Mara is on the rise for the Oklahoma City Thunder this season, and the team hopes that he can continue his development throughout the campaign. Suddenly thrown into the fire, it does seem that the big man is filling the gap in OKC's defensive needs. He's also shining on offense, which is definitely something they need with multiple key stars out with injuries for the Thunder .

From deterring opponents from scoring, blocking shots, crashing the glass, and even creating offensive opportunities, Mara has been a standout for Oklahoma City. He's providing a spark that you wouldn't expect from a rookie. Now he's proven that he can be a consistent player for the team, and that's the hope for him moving forward.

Now averaging 8.3 points, 6.3 rebounds, and 1.8 blocks per game this season, it's clear that Mara has excelled off OKC's bench . His numbers have gone up, and he has garnered a higher usage rate than ever. That says a lot for someone who's supposed to be getting fewer touches as a reserve before getting acclimated to bigger minutes.

But with the Chet Holmgren injury , the Thunder's center spot finds itself with a vacant hole — something that Mara is now taking over in the star's absence. We are at a point where the Spanish center is showcasing his skill set well.

At seven-foot-three, OKC getting Mara in the draft was a huge boon for the franchise on both sides. He's got the potential to be a high-impact defensive anchor alongside Holmgren, which is on-brand with the Thunder's identity. Let's not forget the fact that he's just 21 as well.

As a big man, you'd expect Mara to be a hulk on the glass, much like Victor Wembanyama . This month, the Thunder center has finished with more than five boards in his games. He's averaging 7.8 rebounds in this month alone.

If that's not eye-catching enough for you, then it's worth noting that Mara's rebounding has been essential for the Thunder. In fact, thanks to his efforts, through 11 games, OKC is grabbing nearly five more defensive rebounds per game without Holmgren than with him (36.9 to 32.7). Of course, no Holmgren means Mara and Isaiah Hartenstein get more share at the center spot.

That's a huge difference in cleaning up the glass, which is considered a weakness for OKC by some. With Mara, it does seem that the team can still stay competitive on that end. Now imagine if Holmgren comes back and pairs up with Mara moving forward.

Mara's Shot-Blocking is Elite for a Rookie

To start off his career, Mara has logged 10 straight games with at least one block. He also leads all rookies in total blocks so far this season, which says a lot about his defensive prowess. Of course, some would say that it's less impressive given his height, but his level of hand-eye coordination at that height is hard to come by.

With 20 blocks into the season ( tied for fifth-most ) as of the time of writing, it's not inconceivable that he could receive DPOY votes in his rookie season. Being a reliable defender for OKC, a team that prides itself on defense, is a huge boost to his case.

At this point, he's probably knocking on the Rookie of the Year conversation, but that's still a long shot if we're going solely on his team having the best defense and having the most blocks among rookies.

Mara has so much to offer OKC this season. He's already shown that he can hit a triple on his first attempt (I-Hart has not made a single three in 28 attempts with the Thunder, mind you). Mara is expanding his game. He's shown flashes of playmaking, being able to go coast-to-coast when needed, and his superb shot-blocking ability makes him a huge asset for the team.

But we're just 11 games into the season, and there's so much more for Mara to play, and for OKC to learn how to use him best.

articles.title: Boston Bruins swap sticks for shopping carts for annual holiday tradition
articles.summary: The Boston Bruins traded the ice for the toy aisle Wednesday morning, kicking off the holiday season by shopping for children receiving care at local hospita...
articles.body:
The Boston Bruins traded the ice for the toy aisle Wednesday morning, kicking off the holiday season by shopping for children receiving care at local hospitals.

The entire team visited the Watertown Target for the annual shopping event.

Players picked over $20,000 worth of toys, clothing, and art supplies.

The toys were purchased with donations from the players, coaching staff, and the Boston Bruins Foundation.

The team will visit local hospitals in December and deliver the toys to children who are unable to celebrate the holidays at home.

The annual toy shopping event was first organized 30 years ago by Bruins legend Ray Bourque.

articles.title: Bucs pass rush gets encouraging boost from former first-round pick
articles.summary: Bucs pass rush gets encouraging boost from former first-round pick
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have been waiting for their defensive line to consistently create disruption, and Calijah Kancey's performance against the Chicago Bears was an encouraging sign of what the former first-round pick can bring when he gets going. While Tampa Bay ultimately fell 27-24, Kancey was one of the defensive players who made life difficult for Caleb Williams, helping fuel a defensive performance that produced five turnovers. Kancey finished with three tackles and half a sack, but the numbers don't tell the whole story. His quickness and ability to penetrate the interior created problems for Chicago's offensive line, particularly as the game progressed. Kancey was consistently applying pressure and helped disrupt Williams' rhythm in the second half. After Chicago opened the game with two touchdown drives, Tampa Bay's defense settled in and made it increasingly difficult for Ben Johnson's offense to operate comfortably.

That is the type of impact the Buccaneers need from Kancey. His explosiveness off the snap has always been one of his biggest strengths, and his ability to attack gaps adds a different dimension to Tampa Bay's interior. At 6'1 and 281 pounds, he may not overpower every offensive lineman, but his first-step quickness and ability to get into the backfield can force quarterbacks off their intended spot. Kancey's development is particularly important as Tampa Bay looks for more consistency from its pass rush. He recorded 7.5 sacks in just 12 games during the 2024 season, showing the production he can deliver when healthy. After an injury-shortened 2025 campaign, getting him back to a meaningful level of disruption is a major positive for this defense.

articles.title: Vote for the Journal Sentinel play of the week, Week of Nov. 2-7, 2026
articles.summary: Vote from four nominees for this past week's play of the week: Jeramani Denton (STM), Colin Gardner (Case), Kevin Gomez (CRJ) and Alex Restivo (SH).
articles.body:
What was the best play in Milwaukee-area high school sports last week? You tell us.

This past week featured two plays from playoff football action and two sensational goals on the pitch during the WIAA state soccer tournament and you can decide the best play of the past week by voting from now until noon Saturday, Nov. 14, as many times as you'd like.

We have a submission tool on our Preps Plus portion of the Journal Sentinel website. The location to upload your clips is under the top banner that's labeled " Upload Your Video. " It's a four-step process that will allow you to upload clips from the week across all fall sports. The clips must be trimmed and uploaded to be 30 seconds or shorter in the proper formatting to be eligible for selection. Please submit your clips by the end of the day on Mondays each week to make sure your clip is potentially included to be a nominee.

We also have a step-to-step explainer , along with a link to the Journal Sentinel site, that explains how to upload your own highlight clips for nomination.

If you have any questions about submitting a play of the week nominee, contact Michael Whitlow via email at mwhitlow@gannett.com.

Wauwatosa East vs Whitefish Bay in WIAA Division 2 boys state soccer championship

Jeramani Denton, Saint Thomas More boys soccer

The junior forward scored one of the best goals of the WIAA boys soccer state tournament in the Division 3 state title match Saturday, Nov. 7. With the Cavaliers holding a 1-0 lead late in the first half of STM's 3-1 win over Edgerton , Denton fired a frozen rope of a right-footed strike into the upper 90 at the 35:56 mark to give STM a 2-0 lead on his 15th goal of the season.

Colin Gardner, sr., Racine Case football

Playing in the Division 1 state quarterfinal round for the first time in program history, Gardner drained the biggest kick in Racine Case lore with a walkoff 28-yard field goal as time expired to give the Eagles an improbable 6-3 victory over top-seeded Muskego on the road Friday, Nov. 6, to send Case to the state semifinals.

Kevin Gomez, sr., Cristo Rey Jesuit boys soccer

For the second time in program history in just its 11th year as a WIAA-certified high school, the Cristo Rey Jesuit Trailblazers won the D4 state title with a 2-1 victory over Lake Country Lutheran on Saturday, Nov. 7. The senior forward scored a wonderful goal in the final couple minutes of the first half, chipping the goaltender with a shot attempt a mile high through traffic that gave CRJ a 1-0 lead right before the halftime break for his 33rd goal of the campaign.

Alex Restivo, sr., Sussex Hamilton football

For the third time since 2022, Sussex Hamilton football is on the doorstep of playing for a Division 1 state title. The Chargers advanced to the state semifinal round with a 17-10 victory over defending state champion Arrowhead on the back of an outstanding go-ahead touchdown catch from Alex Restivo in the fourth quarter. The star senior made an amazing diving effort to haul in a Cole Erdmann pass late in the fourth that put Hamilton up for good.

articles.title: Dolphins not moving on from Malik Willis as their starting QB
articles.summary: Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis landed on injured reserve with a groin injury on Tuesday, but he'll take his job back when he's ready.
articles.body:
Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis tried to play through a groin injury the last two weeks, but it was evident that the injury had limited his effectiveness, especially when it came to his mobility.

Speaking to the media on Wednesday, Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said that the imaging revealed that the injury had progressed to the point that the medical staff believed Willis would need time off, which is why they placed him on injured reserve.

While Hafley did say that he hopes that Willis is back after the minimum four games, the quarterback is getting second opinions that could lead to surgery.

Kyle McCord is expected to take over as the team's starting quarterback going forward. However, Hafley told reporters that Willis will take his job back whenever he's healthy and in a position to lead the offense again.

Willis hasn't exactly played inspiring football even when he was healthy, and McCord could end up being a boost for Miami going forward. If that's the case, it would be tough to see the Dolphins switch back to Willis, especialy if McCord wins a couple games.

articles.title: South Knox girls basketball coach suspended for undue influence violation
articles.summary: The violation occurred in May, according to superintendent Jeff Cochren. Additionally, the program is on probation for the remainder of the season.
articles.body:
South Knox girls basketball coach Hollie Anson-Eaves has been suspended two games for violating the Indiana High School Athletic Association's undue influence policy, superintendent Jeff Cochren confirmed Wednesday. Additionally, the program has been placed on probation for the remainder of the season.

Rule 20-1 of the IHSAA bylaws prohibits the recruitment or attempted recruitment of a prospective student through the use of undue influence, which is described as "the act of encouraging or inducing a prospective student to attend a school for athletic purposes."

Anson-Eaves may resume coaching after serving her two-game suspension, but, according to the IHSAA by-laws, must immediately file a report with the IHSAA outlining any corrective actions taken or to be taken by the coach.

In an email to IndyStar and The Courier Press, Cochren said the violation occurred some time in May 2026. The South Knox administration was informed of "the potential for a violation" by the IHSAA in July, and was then "required to respond" to the alleged violation. They did so via written letter in August, then received official notification of the punishment on Nov. 5.

Cochren did not immediately respond to a request for further comment regarding the violation itself.

Anson-Eaves served the first game of her suspension Tuesday, sitting out South Knox's 62-47 win over Class 3A Washington. The Spartans travel to Corydon Central this weekend for the Cluckers Battle at the First Capital. They open the two-day, three-game event against Evansville Central on Friday night.

When reached for comment, an IHSAA spokesperson said per their policy, they do not comment on rules violations or suspensions and instead leave it up to the school if they wish to offer a response.

South Knox added one transfer from Vincennes over the summer, sophomore Azaria Easley, who played for the soccer team in the fall.

Jesse Easley, Azaria's father, addressed allegations of recruiting by SK in a public Facebook post , stating the decision to transfer was rooted in concerns with the Vincennes Lincoln girls soccer program.

Opponents are allowed to drop the Spartans from their 2026-27 schedule without penalty, per IHSAA Bylaw Rule 9-16(b) (3), if alleged to violate Rule 20 concerning undue influence.

Two teams have already canceled games with South Knox: Sectional foe Eastern Greene, its season-opening opponent (Nov. 7), and Vincennes Lincoln, which was scheduled for Jan. 16.

The Spartans have picked up a game vs. Evansville Reitz and is working to add another game to its schedule, according to Cochren.

Anson-Eaves, who will return to the sidelines following her two-game suspension (expected to return Saturday), is 195-114 in 13 seasons at South Knox, with three sectional titles and a Class 2A state championship (2025).

The Spartans are among the favorites to win 2A this season, boasting a veteran lineup headlined by Indiana All-Star candidate Kendal Hill , who averaged 19.2 points, 10.3 rebounds, 5.4 assists and 4.3 steals. Seniors Grace Detweiler, Ellie Burke, Kalissa Lavely and Laya Thomas, and juniors Zoe Glimore and Brynley Millspaugh round out the list of returners.

articles.title: O'Shea proud of how team-mates handled Israel games
articles.summary: Republic of Ireland defender Dara O'Shea is "proud" of how he and his team-mates came through a trying October international window.
articles.body:
Republic of Ireland defender Dara O'Shea said he is "proud" of how he and his team-mates came through a trying October international window.

During a four-game Nations League schedule, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side lost away to Kosovo and drew at home to Austria - who they are preparing to face in return fixtures - but it was two games against Israel which tested their resolve.

O'Shea stepped in as captain in the absence of injured skipper Nathan Collins and the 27-year-old acknowledged it "was a tough situation to be in" as they faced Israel in two games on neutral territory.

The first of those resulted in a 3-0 victory for the Irish in Hungary, a game that looked in doubt the previous day when training was delayed as players took a vote on whether to play - amid protests over the Israel-Gaza war - with goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu making himself unavailable for selection.

The sides drew 1-1 in the second meeting in Serbia and, while the saga proved a challenge for all within the Republic of Ireland squad, O'Shea - who missed the second game for personal reasons - paid tribute to his team-mates for the support he received as stand-in skipper.

"I think I was quite lucky, I am really proud to be part of the group, with some great people in it," said the Ipswich Town captain.

"Even the players playing now as well, they are great leaders themselves. I never felt I was fully alone in having to do anything

"There were always people around me. I always keep level-headed, I don't get too high with the highs or too low with the lows."

He added: "Of course it was a difficult time, it was a time that I had to learn stuff about myself, how I was going to react to things. But I think as a group we did excellently.

"It was a tough situation to be in, but we overcame it as best we could. And I am really proud of the group and the staff."

'Great to have Collins and Coleman back'

Collins is back to lead the team for Saturday's trip to face Austria in Linz and the final League B3 game at home to Kosovo on Tuesday (both 19:45 GMT).

Also part of the squad is Seamus Coleman, who has taken on a 'hybrid role' despite not being named in manager Hallgrimsson's official 24-man squad.

"It's great to have them [Collins and Coleman] back," O'Shea continued.

"It would have been great if they were there in the last camp as well, but we had some really good people in that last camp who were doing great things.

"Nathan's the captain, so it's always great to have him back in. Seamus' knowledge is so, so valuable to us. I think we are a stronger group when we have them two with us."

Coleman has been without a club since leaving Everton at the end of last season, following 17 years with the Toffees.

The 38-year-old defender recently said he is considering retirement but Republic of Ireland assistant coach John O'Shea is delighted to have the Donegal man around the squad.

"It's us helping Seamus and Seamus helping us," O'Shea said of Coleman's role on the training pitch.

"To see the impact he's having, the quality that remains in his ability and the driving and pushing he's doing for everyone in the group has been good to see. Not much has changed."

articles.title: Panthers replenish practice squad after 2 players are poached by Dolphins, Titans
articles.summary: After having two of their players poached, the Panthers added back to their practice squad on Wednesday.
articles.body:
The Carolina Panthers were quick to replenish their practice squad on Wednesday.

This morning, defensive tackle Keith Cooper Jr. and linebacker Mohamoud Diabate were signed off the team's practice squad by the Miami Dolphins and Tennessee Titans, respectively. Carolina then turned around to add wide receiver David Moore and defensive tackle Cam Horsley to the group.

Moore, who was released yesterday , has spent the past three seasons with the Panthers. His first two campaigns saw him record 33 catches for 356 yards and three touchdowns over 21 games.

He's made six appearances here in 2026, with most of his work coming on special teams. The 31-year-old veteran has fielded four punts for 31 yards and eight kickoffs for 168 yards.

Horsley, an undrafted free agent from 2025, split his first two seasons between the Tennessee Titans and Arizona Cardinals . The 6-foot-3, 312-pounder played in one game as a rookie.

Follow @ThePanthersWire on Twitter/X for more Panthers content.

articles.title: Are the Wizards Asking Too Much of Kyshawn George?
articles.summary: The Washington Wizards have been trying to understand what their young roster can become. Kyshawn George is making a strong case for a big role with the Wiza...
articles.body:
The Washington Wizards have been trying to understand what their young roster can become.

Kyshawn George is making a strong case for a big role with the Wizards, but his recent performances have also raised questions about whether the Wizards are putting too much responsibility on him too soon.

George has shown that he can help this team in several areas of the game. The 6-foot-7 forward has become a key piece of the Wizards' offense, using his scoring ability and creative playmaking to make opportunities for himself and his teammates.

Over the last few games, George has become particularly encouraging. George scored 22 points against the Orlando Magic on Nov. 2, followed by 25 points facing the Atlanta Hawks on Nov. 4. He then dropped 33 points in another loss to Atlanta the next game, adding eight assists and five three-pointers.

Those numbers show why Washington has continued to give George opportunities with the ball in his hands. However, his development isn't just about scoring and how many points he can score. The Wizards also need to find the right role for him as he continues to improve in the NBA.

Finding the Right Role for Kyshawn George

One of Kyshawn George's biggest strengths has been his versatility. He's been able to score, defend multiple positions, and help create offense for his teammates. Washington has also been experimenting with using him as a point guard when Trae Young is not playing.

That responsibility has not always been easy.

George recorded eight turnovers against the Toronto Raptors on Oct. 23, a performance that showed some of the challenges of asking him to run the Wizards' offense. He has the ability to make plays, but becoming a good ball handler takes time.

After George's 22-point performance on the Chicago Bulls defense on Oct. 24, Wizards coach Brian Keefe discussed his ability to create more opportunities by getting into the paint.

"You saw him being able to create and get into the paint," Keefe said. "A lot more paint touches for us tonight, which we wanted to emphasize, and he was a catalyst for that."

The comments, reported by Roundtable Sports , show that Washington finds value in what George can bring when he is attacking the basket instead of forcing himself to make all of the plays.

The Wizards should continue giving him opportunities to handle the ball, but they should also recognize when he's most effective.

Trae Young's presence could play an important role in George's development. As an experienced point guard, Young can help take pressure off George while giving him chances to contribute as a secondary playmaker.

George doesn't need to become the team's primary ball handler to be an important part of the offense. Playing alongside Trae Young can allow him to focus on scoring, attacking the basket, and making decisions when defenses give him opportunities.

Washington has also shown that George can help lead the offense when Young is not on the floor. That flexibility is important, especially for a team that is still trying to establish its offensive identity.

The challenge is finding a balance between giving George more responsibility and allowing him to play to his strengths.

The Wizards have invested in developing young players, and George is becoming one of the more important parts of that process. Washington has exercised his fourth-year team option on Nov. 1, showing commitment to keeping him in the team's long-term process.

Through the Wizards' first 11 games, George is averaging 17.9 points, 4.4 rebounds, and 4.9 assists per game.

Still, his recent performances shouldn't mean the Wizards expect him to carry the team every night. George continues to develop as a scorer and playmaker, and there will be nights where he struggles.

Washington needs to give him room to make mistakes while putting him in positions where he can succeed more. Young can help take pressure off, while George continues learning how to become more consistent on offense.

George has shown that he deserves an important role in Washington. The next step the Wizards should take is making sure they can give him the right responsibilities to continue his development.
